entities.summary:
Mentor of Rhodes was a Greek mercenary and later Satrap of the Asiatic coast, who fought both for and against Artaxerxes III of Persia, and is known as the first husband of Barsine, who later became a mistress to Alexander the Great.

He played a significant role in the ancient Mediterranean world, particularly in the Hellenistic period, where he navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between Greek city-states and Persian satrapies.

His experiences and relationships had a lasting impact on the development of the Hellenistic world, shaping the trajectory of Alexander's conquests and the rise of the Seleucid Empire.

One of the most striking aspects of his legacy is the way it continues to influence our understanding of the ancient world, with his story serving as a fascinating case study of the complexities of power, loyalty, and identity in the ancient Mediterranean.
